quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a deep, narrow valley with steep, rocky walls!
quests.question: Canyon
quests.hint: A river often carved this deep, narrow shape into the rock over a very long time.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Canyon is correct because it is a deep valley with steep rocky walls, often carved by a river.
quests.funFact: The Grand Canyon in the United States took millions of years for a river to carve out!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a very steep, tall wall of rock!
quests.question: Cliff
quests.hint: Waves crash against the bottom of this tall, steep rock wall by the sea.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Cliff is correct because it is a very steep, tall wall of rock.
quests.funFact: Many seabirds build their nests safely on the ledges of tall, rocky cliffs!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place that is soft, wet, grassy land soaking in shallow water!
quests.question: Marsh
quests.hint: Tall grasses and reeds grow well in this soggy, wet ground.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Marsh is correct because it is soft, wet, grassy land sitting in shallow water.
quests.funFact: Marshes act like giant sponges that help soak up extra rainwater!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place that is a huge, flat area covered in wild grass!
quests.question: Prairie
quests.hint: This wide open land stretches for miles with hardly a tree in sight.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Prairie is correct because it is a huge, flat area covered in wild grass.
quests.funFact: Prairie grass roots can grow deep enough to survive both drought and fire!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a colorful underwater ridge built by tiny sea creatures!
quests.question: Reef
quests.hint: Many colorful fish make their home around this underwater structure.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Reef is correct because it is a colorful underwater ridge built by tiny sea creatures.
quests.funFact: A reef can take thousands of years to build up to its full size!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a tall yellow flower that follows the Sun across the sky!
quests.question: Sunflower
quests.hint: This flower's big yellow head slowly turns to face the light all day long.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Sunflower is correct because it is a tall yellow flower that turns to follow the Sun.
quests.funFact: A sunflower's middle is actually made of hundreds of tiny little flowers packed together!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a young tree, still thin and just starting to grow!
quests.question: Sapling
quests.hint: This tree is old enough to stand on its own, but still much smaller than a full-grown one.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Sapling is correct because it is a young tree that is still thin and growing.
quests.funFact: A tiny sapling can take many years before it grows into a tall, full-sized tree!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where thick grey clouds cover the whole sky!
quests.question: Overcast
quests.hint: On a day like this, the Sun stays hidden behind clouds from morning to night.
quests.explanation: Yes! Overcast is correct because it describes a sky completely covered in thick grey clouds.
quests.funFact: An overcast sky can still let some sunlight through, even without any blue sky showing!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that is a sudden, very heavy rain!
quests.question: Downpour
quests.hint: This rain falls so hard and fast that you get soaked in just seconds.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Downpour is correct because it is a sudden, very heavy rain.
quests.funFact: A downpour can drop more rain in one hour than a light rain drops in a whole week!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place that is a small group of trees growing together!
quests.question: Grove
quests.hint: This peaceful cluster of trees is smaller and cozier than a big forest.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Grove is correct because it is a small group of trees growing together.
quests.funFact: Some groves are made up of just one single kind of tree, like all olive trees or all orange trees!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object where you can see many colorful layers of rock on the walls!
quests.question: Canyon
quests.hint: Looking down into this deep gap can make you feel very small.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Canyon is correct because its steep walls often show many colorful layers of rock.
quests.funFact: Some canyons are so deep that clouds can form below the rim!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object where you would need climbing gear to reach the top!
quests.question: Cliff
quests.hint: This straight-up-and-down rock face is often found at the edge of the sea or a mountain.
quests.explanation: Great choice! A Cliff is correct because its steep, straight rock face is very hard to climb without gear.
quests.funFact: The tallest sea cliffs in the world rise higher than many skyscrapers!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place where the ground squishes and stays wet nearly all year!
quests.question: Marsh
quests.hint: Many different plants and small creatures make their home in this soggy grassland.
quests.explanation: Great job! A Marsh is correct because its ground stays wet and squishy nearly all year round.
quests.funFact: Marshes help clean water naturally as it slowly flows through all the grass!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place where tall grass waves gently in an open, endless wind!
quests.question: Prairie
quests.hint: This wide grassy land has very few trees to block the wind.
quests.explanation: Great choice! A Prairie is correct because it is an open, grassy land where the wind moves freely.
quests.funFact: Prairies once covered a huge part of central North America!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that protects the coastline by breaking up big ocean waves!
quests.question: Reef
quests.hint: This underwater wall of coral helps keep the water near the beach calmer.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Reef is correct because it breaks up big waves and protects the coastline.
quests.funFact: Reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, but support huge amounts of sea life!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object with a big brown center full of tasty seeds!
quests.question: Sunflower
quests.hint: Birds love to snack on the seeds found in the middle of this tall yellow flower.
quests.explanation: Great choice! A Sunflower is correct because its big brown center is full of seeds.
quests.funFact: Some sunflowers can grow taller than a grown-up, reaching over ten feet high!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that grows taller every year after sprouting from a seed!
quests.question: Sapling
quests.hint: This young, thin tree needs plenty of sunlight and water to keep growing strong.
quests.explanation: Great job! A Sapling is correct because it keeps growing taller every year after starting as a seed.
quests.funFact: People often plant rows of these young trees to grow a brand new forest!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event when the whole sky turns a dull, cloudy grey!
quests.question: Overcast
quests.hint: This kind of day feels cooler because clouds are blocking the Sun's warmth.
quests.explanation: That's right! Overcast is correct because the whole sky turns a dull grey, blocking direct sunlight.
quests.funFact: Overcast skies often happen just before or after a rainy day!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where rain pours down so hard it's difficult to see far ahead!
quests.question: Downpour
quests.hint: Streets can quickly fill up with puddles during this heavy kind of rain.
quests.explanation: Great job! A Downpour is correct because it pours down so hard that it's hard to see far.
quests.funFact: Some downpours end almost as quickly as they start, lasting just a few minutes!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place where a small cluster of trees offers a shady resting spot!
quests.question: Grove
quests.hint: This little patch of trees is perfect for a quiet picnic in the shade.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Grove is correct because its small cluster of trees offers cool, shady rest.
quests.funFact: Ancient people often held important meetings in the shade of a quiet grove!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that a river slowly cuts deeper into the rock every single year!
quests.question: Canyon
quests.hint: This giant rocky gap keeps getting a tiny bit deeper as water flows through it.
quests.explanation: Great job! A Canyon is correct because flowing water slowly cuts it deeper into the rock over time.
quests.funFact: It can take millions of years for a canyon to form from a river's flowing water!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object with a sudden, steep drop straight down!
quests.question: Cliff
quests.hint: You should always stay a safe distance back from the edge of this tall, steep rock.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Cliff is correct because it has a sudden, steep drop straight down.
quests.funFact: Some cliffs formed underwater, long before the ocean level dropped to reveal them!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place that sits between dry land and open, deep water!
quests.question: Marsh
quests.hint: This soggy, grassy place is neither fully dry land nor a deep lake.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Marsh is correct because it sits between dry land and open water, staying wet and grassy.
quests.funFact: Marshes are one of the most important homes for young fish and water birds!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place that is flat, grassy, and stretches all the way to the horizon!
quests.question: Prairie
quests.hint: You could walk for a very long time here before spotting a single tree.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Prairie is correct because it is a flat, grassy land stretching far into the distance.
quests.funFact: Many prairies naturally burn every few years, which actually helps new grass grow back!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object made of thousands of tiny connected coral skeletons!
quests.question: Reef
quests.hint: This underwater home looks like a rocky garden full of color.
quests.explanation: Great job! A Reef is correct because it is made of thousands of tiny connected coral skeletons.
quests.funFact: The biggest reef in the world can be seen from outer space!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that grows a bright yellow ring of petals around a dark center!
quests.question: Sunflower
quests.hint: Farmers grow whole fields of this cheerful yellow flower for its seeds and oil.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Sunflower is correct because it grows a bright yellow ring of petals around a dark center.
quests.funFact: Sunflower fields can stretch out in bright yellow for as far as you can see!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is too young and thin to have thick, strong branches yet!
quests.question: Sapling
quests.hint: This young tree will need many more years before it looks like a full-grown tree.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Sapling is correct because it is still too young to have thick, strong branches.
quests.funFact: Some saplings grow fastest in the few years right after they first sprout!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where you cannot see even a little patch of blue sky!
quests.question: Overcast
quests.hint: Clouds spread out and cover every part of the sky on a day like this.
quests.explanation: Great choice! Overcast is correct because clouds spread out to cover the entire sky.
quests.funFact: Photographers sometimes love overcast days because the soft light has no harsh shadows!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that can quickly fill up a bucket left outside!
quests.question: Downpour
quests.hint: This heavy rain falls fast enough to make a loud drumming sound on a rooftop.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Downpour is correct because it falls fast and heavy enough to quickly fill things up.
quests.funFact: The heaviest downpours on Earth happen in warm, tropical places near the equator!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place that is smaller and friendlier than a big, wide forest!
quests.question: Grove
quests.hint: You could walk all the way through this small patch of trees in just a few minutes.
quests.explanation: Great choice! A Grove is correct because it is a small, friendly patch of trees, smaller than a forest.
quests.funFact: Many groves are planted on purpose by people, unlike wild forests that grow on their own!
